correctness.rationale: For Z=sin(pi U), log Z is square-integrable (near the endpoints it has only logarithmic singularities). Thus AM–GM gives a uniform L2 bound for the log of the sample mean and log forcing is integrable. Birkhoff applies to the Haar-ergodic translation; away from the null orbit of the pinch the product of fiber derivatives gives the exponent. The tanh inequality gives the claimed subcritical upper rate simultaneously for all permitted positive initial heights. Leave-one-out means differ unless all samples coincide, so strict Jensen orders the thresholds; ordinary strict Jensen bounds every threshold below by pi/2. For K2, reflecting one uniform angle sends cos((u-v)/2) to sin((u+v)/2). The triangular law of the angle sum reduces the average log to (16/pi^2) times the integral of s log(sin s) on [0,pi/2]. The Abel expansion integrates each cosine with coefficient [((-1)^n-1)/(4n^2)], giving -2 log 2+7 zeta(3)/pi^2 with dominated convergence for the log singularity. For large d, raw moments 2/pi, 1/2, 4/(3pi) give v and tau in the paper; tau=(48-5pi^2)/(3pi^3)<0, so both Taylor coefficients are positive directly. Centered-index partitions give moments of orders 5 and 6 of size O(d^-3), and order 8 of size O(d^-4), implying the stated seventh absolute-moment bound. The exponential tail and uniform log L2 bound justify discarding the complement of the Taylor interval. The adjacent-dimension inequalities at the first strict crossing sandwich delta between threshold values at d_* and d_*-1, yielding c1/d_*+O(d_*^-2), including equality at an earlier dimension. The fresh one-dimensional quadrature gives K2≈1.70529405808, and moment quadrature gives c1≈0.11685027495 and c2≈0.05968448804. Source checker inspected, not executed: its grid refinements are all at d=2, and a2>a1 checks the sign of c2 rather than the accuracy of the asymptotic at higher d. The printed K2 in VERIFICATION.md is the finite odd-series sum, not the exact value at its last digits. The analytic proof, not those checks, validates the all-dimension claims.
residual_risks: No nonlinear classification at neutral equality; no finite-time probability law or assertion that a positive zero-graph exponent by itself determines all initial conditions.

value.rationale: Dimension already parametrizes a standard forcing model, but it was not merely a fixed label here: every intermediate coupling selects a unique last nonpositive/first positive boundary in dimension. Strict ordering, the explicit two-dimensional benchmark and the small-delta crossover scale provide quantitative guidance unavailable from a generic integral criterion. The result is scoped to zero-graph transverse exponents rather than oversold as a classification of all attractors.
